sentences.text:
On The 5 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 39770 of 2025
 Ayush Jha
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Mayank Sharma - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Vipin Singh Thakur -Advocate for the objector.
 Shri G.S. Thakur - Government Advocate for the responde

Order 
This is repeat (fifth) application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.315/2024 registered at Police Station, Lordganj, District Jabalpur for the offences punishable under Sections 376,
376(2)(n), 376-D, 386 and 506 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3/4, 5/(L)/6 of the POCSO Act.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that though there is allegation against the applicant that he has prepared obscene video, however, no video has been recovered from his mobile.

More over, he has submitted that the other co-accused persons have been enlarged on bail and now the deposition of the victim is also recorded, where also she has not supported any allegation made against the present applicant and, therefore, he prays for consideration of his bail application.

4. Per contra , learned counsel for the State has drawn the attention of this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63595 2 MCRC-39770-2025 Court towards the order passed by this Court in fourth bail application of the present applicant passed in M.Cr.C. 20252/2025 on 05.08. 2025,
whereby similar contentions raised by the counsel for the applicant was examined by the Court and discussed in detailed and, therefore, he submitted that as such no change in circumstances has taken place and such repeated attempt should not be entertained.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for objector has also drawn the attention of this Court to the deposition of victim and submits that specific role was played by the present applicant which is coming from the examination-in-chief and, therefore, submitted that considering the other material available on record and considering the fact that there is specific allegation against the applicant that he has made video and on that basis, the other co-accused persons have misused the video by indulging in such offence repeatedly and, therefore, he has submitted that discretion should not be exercised in favour of the present applicant.
Hence, counsel submits that no case for grant of bail is made out against the applicant.
6. I have considered the rival submissions made at the Bar.

This Court is conscious that the applicant is a young boy of 18 years, but considering the conduct of the applicant which reflects the present atmosphere prevailing in the society and also impact of the electronic gazette available to the youngsters, which they are misusing like anything knowingly or unknowingly entering into such criminal activity of which the present case is a classic example of the same.
It is also required to be noted that the coordinate Bench has rejected the application of the same accused by discussing all contentions raised in the present application by order dated 05.08.2025.

The observations made by the co-ordinate Bench in paragraphs 4 to 12 of the said order are reproduced as under:-
"4.
Learned

Senior counsel for applicant submits that allegation against NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63595 3 MCRC-39770-2025 present applicant is that he prepared obscene video and obscene photographs of prosecutrix.
Learned Senior Counsel for applicant also submits that in the instant case, incident is said to have occurred from 15.11.2021 to 10.06.2024 and FIR has been lodged on 21.06.2024.
Main allegation is against co-accused Dev Arya, who established physical relations on the false pretext of marriage with prosecutrix.

It is also urged that prosecutrix's statements were recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. on 23.06.2024 and Section 164 of Cr.P.C. recorded on 22.06.2024 and therein, no allegations have been leveled against present applicant.
It is only in prosecutrix's statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. on 24.6.2024 that there is a reference to obscene video and photographs prepared by the applicant.

It is also urged that in the instant case,
Investigation Officer has been examined and Cyber Forensic Officer, Priyanka Agrawal (PW-4) has been examined.
As per testimony of Priyanka Agrawal, no obscene video has been found in mobile recovered from applicant.
It is also urged that in FIR, there is no reference to any obscene video or photographs prepared by the applicant.
In FIR, only allegation is that prosecutrix was having relation with Dev Arya and he established physical relation with him.

5. Learned Senior Counsel for the applicant also submits that there are material omissions, contradictions and discrepancies in prosecutrix's statement recorded in the Court as well as her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., it is urged that in statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. on 24.6.2024, allegation of extortion is leveled against Ashmit and it has also been alleged that Hamid established physical relations with prosecutrix.

It is also urged that Ashmit's second bail application has been allowed on 15.10.2024 and Hamid has Ayush Jha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98001804/
2 also been released on bail on 2.08.2024.

sentences.text: Applicant is in jail since 30.06.2024.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the application.
7. Heard.
Perused record of the case.

8. Perused record of the case reveals that earlier applicant's bail applications were dismissed vide order dated 09.08.2024, 12.11.2024 and 22.3.2025 on merits and present bail application has been filed on 02.05.2025.
9.

It is correct that co-accused Hamid has been released on bail on 2.08.2024 and Ashmit has been released on bail on 15.10.20204 but present applicant's bail applications have been dismissed on merits even after co-accused Hamid and Ashmit were released on bail.

Further, there are observations of this Court in order dated 9.08.2024 passed in MCRC No.33386/2024 that applicant cannot claim any parity NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63595 4 MCRC-39770-2025 with the case of Mohd.Hamid Mansoori.

10. This Court has gone through and examined the FIR lodged by prosecutrix and prosecutrix's statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. on 23.06.2024 and Section 164 of Cr.P.C. statement recorded on 22.6.2024 and also Section 164 of Cr.P.C. statement recorded on 24.06.2024 as well as record of the case.

11. Hence, there appears to be no substantial change in circumstances of the case,
after dismissal of earlier bail applications of applicant.
12. It is also well established that Court testimonies of prosecution witnesses cannot be assessed and evaluated on merits at the stage of consideration of bail application."

7. Considering such tendency to file repeated application by asking bail, though there is no substantial change in circumstances, requires to be discarded otherwise also when earlier order passed on merit by dealing with all the contentions raised in the petition that order is not challenged in the higher forum.
Considering that aspect also and the fact that there is strong prima facie case against the present applicant, no discretion should be exercised in favour of applicant.

Accordingly,
this application is dismissed.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT) JUDGE b Ayush Jha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98001804/
